item.title: Cineplexity: Can Hollywood make video game movies that stand on their own?
item.description: Hollywood wants to tap into the built-in audience for video games. NPR's Stephen Thompson and Vincent Acovino discuss what it takes to make a video game adaptation that works beyond its fan base.
item.content:encoded: Hollywood wants to tap into the built-in audience for video games. NPR's Stephen Thompson and Vincent Acovino discuss what it takes to make a video game adaptation that works beyond its fan base.
item.dc:creator: Marc Rivers

item.title: The Amazon's future is on the ballot in Brazil. Many voters aren't focused on it
item.description: Brazil's environment is a global concern. But on the campaign trail, it's struggling to get voters' attention.
item.content:encoded: Brazil's environment is a global concern. But on the campaign trail, it's struggling to get voters' attention.

item.title: What does marathon training do to your body? A reporter becomes the test subject
item.description: Before running the New York City Marathon, NPR's Elissa Nadworny gets a bone scan, blood work and a treadmill test to settle a question from Mom: Is this bad for my body?

item.title: In 'Ply,' Hernán Díaz imagines what we become after the world we know
item.description: Pulitzer prize winner Hernán Díaz' new book 'Ply' follows a young woman who siphons electricity to power punk shows in a re-wilded world. Díaz tells NPR how the novel came to examine selfhood, identity and intimacy.

item.title: Supreme Court starts a new term with a case about who pays for climate damage
item.description: The Supreme Court starts its new term with a Colorado county's claim that an oil refinery worsened climate change. The ruling could determine whether similar cases can move forward.

item.title: How much are AI data centers adding to your electricity bill?
item.description: Americans are worried AI data centers will raise their electricity bills. Congress has come up with a plan to protect ratepayers, but there's no easy way to find out what AI is costing them.

item.title: Brazil's election could shift its ties with the U.S. and China
item.description: Brazil is a global supplier of oil, soybeans and critical minerals. Americas Quarterly editor in chief Brian Winter explains how Brazil's presidential election could impact trade with the U.S. and China.

item.title: Brazil votes, with Lula facing Bolsonaro's son
item.description: In Brazil, President Lula da Silva faces Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the jailed former president, in a tight race. If neither wins more than half the votes they'll face each other again on Oct. 25.

item.title: 'It's not just a Cornell problem': Students speak out about sexual assault
item.description: Women are posting videos hashtagged #IAmJaneDoe to support the woman suing Cornell. Students across the country say her case raises concerns about safety on campus.

item.title: For some Brazilians, this election is a vote on Trump
item.description: President Trump says he's been having success winning races in Latin America. As Brazilian voters go to the polls, they're also deciding how much influence Trump should have in their country.
